issue_context.body:

  - If you need additional help with this template, please refer to https://www.home-assistant.io/help/reporting_issues/
  - Make sure you are running the latest version of Home Assistant before reporting an issue: https://github.com/home-assistant/core/releases
  - Do not report issues for integrations if you are using custom components or integrations.
  - Provide as many details as possible. Paste logs, configuration samples and code into the backticks.
  DO NOT DELETE ANY TEXT from this template! Otherwise, your issue may be closed without comment.
-->
## The problem
<!-- 
  Describe the issue you are experiencing here to communicate to the
  maintainers. Tell us what you were trying to do and what happened.
-->

When initializing the [Epson Projector](https://www.home-assistant.io/integrations/epson/) integration, the `media_player.epson_projector` shows as "Not Available." The error is inconsistent and can sometimes be fixed by restarting HA, but not always. The service `epson.select_cmode` loads even if `media_player.epson_projector` does not.

In my testing, I removed the `customize.yaml` `!include` I described below but didn't seem to change anything after several restarts. ~~and it seemed to work more often than not while still being inconsistent.~~

The integration uses [this library, for reference](https://github.com/pszafer/epson_projector).

## Environment
<!--
  Provide details about the versions you are using, which helps us to reproduce
  and find the issue quicker. Version information is found in the
  Home Assistant frontend: Developer tools -> Info.
-->

- Home Assistant Core release with the issue: 0.113.3
- Last working Home Assistant Core release (if known): 0.112 (venv)
- Operating environment (OS/Container/Supervised/Core): OS
- Integration causing this issue: [Epson Projector](https://www.home-assistant.io/integrations/epson/)
- Link to integration documentation on our website: https://www.home-assistant.io/integrations/epson/

## Problem-relevant `configuration.yaml`
<!--
  An example configuration that caused the problem for you. Fill this out even
  if it seems unimportant to you. Please be sure to remove personal information
  like passwords, private URLs and other credentials.
-->
My config for the integration:

```yaml
media_player:
  - platform: epson
    host: ip.ad.dr.ess
    name: 'Epson Projector'

#also relevant
homeassistant:
  customize: !include customize.yaml
```

Customize.yaml section:

```yaml
media_player.epson_projector:
  cmode_list: '["Bright Cinema","Cinema","Natural","Dynamic"]'
```

Removing the `customize.yaml` `!include` seemed to allow the integration to load at least once, but would continue to fail after restarting.

## Traceback/Error logs
<!--
  If you come across any trace or error logs, please provide them.
-->

```txt
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "/usr/local/lib/python3.8/site-packages/epson_projector/main.py", line 127, in send_request
    async with self.websession.get(
  File "/usr/local/lib/python3.8/site-packages/aiohttp/client.py", line 1012, in __aenter__
    self._resp = await self._coro
  File "/usr/local/lib/python3.8/site-packages/aiohttp/client.py", line 504, in _request
    await resp.start(conn)
  File "/usr/local/lib/python3.8/site-packages/aiohttp/client_reqrep.py", line 847, in start
    message, payload = await self._protocol.read()  # type: ignore  # noqa
  File "/usr/local/lib/python3.8/site-packages/aiohttp/streams.py", line 591, in read
    await self._waiter
asyncio.exceptions.CancelledError

During handling of the above exception, another exception occurred:

Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "/usr/src/homeassistant/homeassistant/helpers/entity_platform.py", line 320, in _async_add_entity
    await entity.async_device_update(warning=False)
  File "/usr/src/homeassistant/homeassistant/helpers/entity.py", line 463, in async_device_update
    await self.async_update()  # type: ignore
  File "/usr/src/homeassistant/homeassistant/components/epson/media_player.py", line 142, in async_update
    is_turned_on = await self._projector.get_property(POWER)
  File "/usr/local/lib/python3.8/site-packages/epson_projector/main.py", line 95, in get_property
    response = await self.send_request(
  File "/usr/local/lib/python3.8/site-packages/epson_projector/main.py", line 138, in send_request
    return response
  File "/usr/local/lib/python3.8/site-packages/async_timeout/__init__.py", line 45, in __exit__
    self._do_exit(exc_type)
  File "/usr/local/lib/python3.8/site-packages/async_timeout/__init__.py", line 92, in _do_exit
    raise asyncio.TimeoutError
asyncio.exceptions.TimeoutError
```

## Additional information
comments:
Additional information here - 

I was able to connect to the projector and turn it on and off directly using the [epson_projector](https://github.com/pszafer/epson_projector) library bypassing HA.

This is the same as #30624, which was closed. However, the issue still persists. 

The hack shared by @workingmanrob is to edit `epson_projector/main.py` and change

```python
response = await self.send_request(
            timeout=timeout,
            params=EPSON_KEY_COMMANDS[command],
            type='json_query')
```

to 

```python
response = await self.send_request(
            timeout=6000, #overwrite timeout time
            params=EPSON_KEY_COMMANDS[command],
            type='json_query')
```

in this function: https://github.com/pszafer/epson_projector/blob/34fa97f3bbb046bf4f5772b304e4193e2d167671/epson_projector/main.py#L89-L104


The standard timeouts for `epson_projector` are:

```python
TIMEOUT_TIMES = {
    'TURN_ON': 40,
    'TURN_OFF': 10,
    'SOURCE': 5,
    'ALL': 3
}
```

This request triggers from the `/components/epson/media_player.py` line 142: https://github.com/home-assistant/core/blob/7c117452babe5ee889f0233c25487b1daefc27ba/homeassistant/components/epson/media_player.py#L142

So the timeout for this request ends up being `3`, which is seconds per [source](https://github.com/aio-libs/async-timeout) and the command that is called is `POWER = "PWR"`.


My attempt to fix this is:

- Add the `epson_projector` module to `custom_components/epson_projector`.
- Update `epson_projector/const.py` to include a new timeout time for power as below:
  
  ```python
  TIMEOUT_TIMES = {
      'TURN_ON': 40,
      'TURN_OFF': 10,
      'PWR': 600,
      'SOURCE': 5,
      'ALL': 3
  }
  ```
- Restart HA
- Realize nothing changed because `custom_components` doesn't affect `site-packages`
- Change `const.py` directly through ssh access
- Restart HA
- **It works!**

| Time Value | Success/Failure |
| --- | --- |
| 3s | Failure |
| 6000s | Success (Per @workingmanrob) |
| 600s | Success |
| 10s | Success |
| 5s | Success |


For now, I'll leave my configuration as 10s and see if it has any issues in the future. Not going to close this issue because I don't know if this result implies an issue with the `epson_projector` library or with HA's handling of an error like this.


I have submitted a [pull request ](https://github.com/pszafer/epson_projector/pull/4) at the `epson_projector` library to increase the timeout to 10s.
